Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Human awareness is perpetually obscured by this unquenchable enemy in the form of desire, which burns like an insatiable fire and can never be satisfied through indulgence.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The false belief that satisfying an unhealthy desire will extinguish it.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna warns that desire acts like fire (duspurenanalena)—adding fuel (indulgence) only makes the flame burn hotter, keeping pure wisdom obscured.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna sees the futility of trying to pacify compulsive cravings through endless indulgence.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Insatiable Cravings: Desires that grow stronger rather than weaker when indulged
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.The Hedonic Treadmill: The endless cycle of seeking temporary pleasure without lasting satisfaction
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Delusion of Indulgence: Falsely believing that giving in to an urge will permanently eliminate it

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Avrtam jnanam etena jnanino nitya-vairina (Wisdom is covered by this perpetual enemy of the wise)
Kama-rupena kaunteya duspurenanalena ca (In the form of desire, an insatiable fire)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Lust is the perpetual enemy of spiritual progress. It covers wisdom and acts like a fire that grows hotter the more fuel (sense gratification) is fed into it.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Feeding an addiction or destructive impulse never cures it; it only reinforces the habit loop. Long-term peace requires breaking the cycle of indulgence rather than trying to satisfy insatiable demands.
